quote.text: Everything is worth what its purchaser will pay for it.
quote.author: Publilius Syrus, Sententiae, first century BC

stories.headline: Trump says Washington stops $4bn a year in military aid to Israel
stories.dek: The memorandum signed under Obama says $3.8bn and runs to September 2028, and Netanyahu’s office declined to comment — he has been a caretaker since 27 October.

stories.headline: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum for $115bn; its own shares fall 32%
stories.dek: The price is 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share. By Tuesday’s close those were worth $773.87, not the $1,132.43 announced on Monday.

stories.headline: The Bank of Thailand’s horse list runs to 246,000 names and 3.56 million accounts
stories.dek: A third of them have no complainant. In Thailand a delivery rider has been frozen since April over a transfer of 140 baht, and no court hears an appeal against a listing.

stories.headline: SATS sends office staff to the baggage belt as MOM investigates 45 contractors
stories.dek: The ministry found Employment Pass holders handling bags and says the declared salaries were false. A day later, SATS asked desk staff to volunteer for 2.5-hour shifts.

stories.headline: A hardware-shop saw is harder than Lie-Nielsen’s, and cannot be sharpened
stories.dek: Lie-Nielsen tempers its plate to 50–52 on the Rockwell scale so a file can cut it. A hardware-shop saw runs 68 to 71, and is thrown away.

stories.headline: Apple’s OLED iPad mini reaches Singapore on Friday from S$999
stories.dek: Apple sorts the chip by storage size: only the S$1,449 model carries six processor cores and two on-device AI units, against five and one beneath it.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Heritage Chronograph
stories.headline: H. Moser limits its new Heritage Chronograph to 100 pieces at CHF 29,200
stories.dek: About S$45,600 for a steel 42mm watch good to 30 metres. The caseback is engraved “LIMITED 100 PCS”; the maker’s own product page gives no edition size at all.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · A Documentary At No. 1
stories.headline: A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary topped the US box office for a third weekend
stories.dek: It took $11,445,629 from 3,243 theatres, reaching $64.7m. No documentary has led the American box office since Michael Moore in 2004.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Puberty And Mood
stories.headline: A Beijing study ties parents’ puberty talk to lower depression in girls
stories.dek: The Beijing Normal University team followed 1,977 seventh-graders for a year, mean age 12.73. Early puberty predicted lower mood only in girls whose parents had not explained it.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Real Rate
stories.headline: Oil nearly doubled in a year and American inflation expectations fell one basis point
stories.dek: The ten-year Treasury yield rose 82 basis points over twelve months. The real yield rose 83. Every bit of the move was the real rate; none of it was inflation.

stories.headline: A Bally of 1969 is easier to repair than a Stern of 2026
stories.dek: Stern sells thirty-four titles from Elk Grove Village, Illinois, at $6,999 to $12,999. A Bally from 1969 has no computer in it at all, which is why people keep them.

stories.headline: A São Paulo meta-analysis finds soy and pea shakes match whey for muscle
stories.dek: The São Paulo team pooled five trials and 372 untrained adults, all scanned. The difference in lean mass was 0.35kg in plant protein’s favour, and statistically nothing.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Two Ballots This Fortnight
stories.headline: KATSEYE opens its Singapore presale on 10 November without publishing a price
stories.dek: Japan’s Jump Festa ballot closes at 17:59 on 16 November, and it is free. Sumo’s January advance sale opens 5 December, with the price table still empty.
